title: Release Trail
brief: After release {{rel}} of the Meridian Digital scheduling platform, three customers report that recurring appointments are duplicated. You are asked to trace release {{rel}} through its records and define which releases, environments, and customers are affected. You have 12 visit points.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Change ticket for the recurrence engine
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Release record for {{rel}} lists the build number 2291, the included change tickets, and the approver.
evidence.whyItMatters: Release identification links the deployed software to its contents.
evidence.missedExplanation: This record is the map for the trail.
evidence.falseFindingNote: A complete release record is conforming.

evidence.text: Deployment log: {{rel}} went to the EU region as build 2291 but to the US region as build 2293. The release record mentions only 2291.
evidence.whyItMatters: The organization must be able to identify exactly what is deployed where. Two builds under one release name break traceability and widen the scope.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare build numbers across every region in the deployment log.

evidence.text: Change tickets: 12 tickets are included, each with an approver and linked tests.
Change ticket CHG-881 for the recurrence engine was edited after approval to add a second fix; there is no re-approval.
evidence.whyItMatters: Changes must be reviewed and approved as they will be released. An unreviewed addition can introduce defects.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check edit dates against approval dates.

evidence.text: Regression run for {{rel}}: 6 recurrence tests were skipped with the note "flaky"; sign-off was given with no reference to the skipped tests.
evidence.whyItMatters: Release should follow completion of planned verification, or an authorized decision that considers what was not done.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read skipped and failed counts, not only the pass rate.

evidence.text: Test case library has no test for recurring appointments that cross a daylight-saving date, although requirement REQ-77 names it.
evidence.whyItMatters: Design verification should cover the requirements stated for the design.
evidence.missedExplanation: Trace each requirement to at least one test.

evidence.text: Date-handling library was upgraded from 3.2 to 4.0 in {{rel}}; the upgrade has a ticket but no review of the library's change notes.
evidence.whyItMatters: Externally provided components should be checked for their effect. Here a ticket exists, so it is an opportunity to strengthen the review.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask how third-party component updates are evaluated.

evidence.text: Support tickets: 3 customer reports are linked to problem record PRB-56 with customer and region noted.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer feedback is captured and linked.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence that helps define scope.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Linking tickets to a problem record is good practice.

evidence.text: Release manager: "Build 2293 was a quick hotfix for the US time zone. We did not raise a ticket; it was urgent." (note 4)
evidence.whyItMatters: Every change to released software needs a record and an approval, including urgent ones.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask about anything not in the register.

evidence.text: Rollback plan for {{rel}} is documented and was tested in staging.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The rollback plan is sound. Conforming.

evidence.text: The release note uses informal wording, "squashed a few bugs", for 2 items.
evidence.whyItMatters: Tone of a release note is not a requirement unless the customer contract sets one.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Informal wording is a style matter, not a nonconformity.

evidence.text: The support dashboard uses red and green colors only.
evidence.whyItMatters: Dashboard design is not a quality requirement in this case.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Dashboard colors do not affect conformity of the release.

decisions.prompt: Which deployments and customers are in scope for containment?
options: Only the 3 customers who reported the fault
All customers on build 2291 and build 2293 in both regions, with priority for recurring appointments that cross daylight-saving dates
Every release since the platform started
decisions.rationale: The edited change ticket, the skipped tests, and the untracked hotfix mean both builds are in scope. The missing daylight-saving test points to which data to check first.

containment: Pause further deployment of {{rel}} and assess rollback for affected regions
Notify affected customers and identify duplicated appointments
correction: Remove duplicate appointments with customer agreement and record build 2293 in the release register
cause: Urgent fixes bypass change records, and sign-off allows skipped tests without an authorized decision
corrective: Require a ticket and approval for every build, including hotfixes; block sign-off while planned tests are skipped without approval
effectiveness: Compare deployment logs with the release register for the next five releases

debriefText.found: You traced the release by build number, not by its name.
debriefText.missed: The most-missed card is the second build number in the deployment log. Read build numbers region by region.
debriefText.falseFinding: Informal release note wording and dashboard colors do not break a requirement.
